evidence.quote: The primary mission of ZYZZsat is to image the whole Great Barrier Reef in visible bands at 5 m resolution
The operator is the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS)

criteria.reasoning: All required items addressed: primary mission, rationale with cited context, single-spacecraft justification, operator and multiple customers. Detailed and well referenced; only slightly brief on funding/rationale depth.

evidence.quote: The baseline is an SSMS rideshare flight on Vega C from Kourou in early 2025
There are six passes each day, three in the evening and three in the morning (UTC)

criteria.reasoning: Launch, orbit (with correct J2 sun-sync hand calc verified), elements, manoeuvres, ground station, access frequency, duration and EOL all covered with STK screenshots, access tables, hand calculations and references. Link budget admittedly missing, a minor gap.

evidence.quote: A 600 km sun-synchronous orbit at 97.79° inclination gives the same morning lighting on every pass

criteria.reasoning: Conclusions follow directly from the evidence and honestly identify limitations and further work; specific and useful, though brief.

evidence.quote: This report presents the design of ZYZZsat (Z-axis/Y-axis Zeroed Zoning Satellite), a single Earth observation microsatellite
Figure 2: Inclination required for a sun-synchronous orbit as a function of altitude.

criteria.reasoning: Clear structure, executive summary, numbered/labelled figures and tables, consistent IEEE-style citations matching the bibliography, good grammar. Minor: some references (e.g. [15]) are vague.

technical_issues.issue: Accesses computed with no elevation constraint; usable-time estimate above 10° is approximated rather than re-run in STK.
No X-band link budget, acknowledged by the author.
Decay analysis uses a single mean density; solar-cycle variation only discussed qualitatively.
Vega C flight record stated as of 2020; by a 2025 launch the comparison would need updating (minor).

overall: An excellent, technically sound mission design report. Correct hand calculations (sun-sync inclination, azimuth, period, decay, data budget) verified, well supported by STK evidence, clearly written and properly referenced. Minor gaps: link budget and elevation-constrained access analysis.
